card.title: B7A2 RYUSEI
card.flavorText: The Aichi B7A Ryusei (Ryusei means "Shooting Star" in Japanese) was a Japanese carrier borne torpedo dive bomber that was produced during WWII for the Imperial Japanese Navy Air Service. The B7A Ryusei was a big and powerful aircraft and was intended to be used on a new type of carrier (Taihō-class) which could handle larger aircraft. The problem was that once the B7A entered production and was ready for service in 1944, there was only one carrier modern enough to handle the aircraft: the Taihō. And to make matters worse, the Taihō carrier was sunk during the Battle of the Philippine Sea, before any of the B7A’s were embarked. After this, some of the B7A’s operated from land, but they saw limited service until the war ended in 1945. A total of 105 B7A2 Ryusei were produced, plus a handful of other variants.
